articles.title: Glucose-Lowering Therapies in Type 2 Diabetes-Associated Sarcopenia: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence and a Muscle-Centred Framework.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognised as a clinically important comorbidity in diabetes mellitus, particularly in older adults and individuals with long-standing type 2 diabetes. Because skeletal muscle is the principal site of insulin-stimulated glucose disposal, declines in muscle mass, quality, strength and physical performance may exacerbate insulin resistance and glycaemic instability and increase the risks of frailty, disability, falls, fractures, cardiovascular events and mortality. Contemporary glucose-lowering therapies have transformed diabetes care through established cardiorenal benefits and weight reduction, yet skeletal muscle outcomes are rarely prespecified or systematically assessed in pivotal trials. This evidence gap is especially relevant for weight-reducing agents such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, which are often associated with reductions in dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived or bioelectrical impedance analysis-derived lean-mass estimates. However, these changes should be interpreted cautiously, as they often occur in the context of overall weight loss and may be influenced by alterations in body water. In addition, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry- or dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived lean-mass estimates do not directly quantify contractile skeletal muscle. Accordingly, reductions in lean-mass estimates alone are insufficient to infer clinically meaningful muscle loss without concurrent assessment of muscle strength or physical performance. This narrative review summarises the bidirectional mechanisms linking diabetes and sarcopenia and appraises major glucose-lowering drug classes from a muscle-centred perspective. It integrates mechanistic insights with human evidence on muscle-relevant outcomes, including body composition, strength and physical performance, and addresses practical safety and monitoring considerations in sarcopenia-prone phenotypes, including sarcopenic obesity. We also propose a pragmatic, hypothesis-generating Cardiorenal-Muscle Quadrant Framework that considers glycaemic efficacy and cardiorenal benefit alongside muscle reserve, functional status and treatment-related risks, with emphasis on functional monitoring, resistance exercise, nutritional optimisation and individualised glycaemic targets in older or frail adults.

articles.title: Dysregulated Metal Homeostasis in Alzheimer's Disease: From Pathological Modulators to Therapeutic Targets.
articles.abstract: The "metal ion hypothesis" of Alzheimer's disease (AD) has gained widespread acceptance, but translating this understanding into effective therapies remains elusive. This likely stems from a simplistic understanding of metal homeostasis as merely a matter of "excess and deficiency." This article reviews the context-dependent roles of iron, copper, zinc, aluminum, and manganese in the pathogenesis of AD, with a particular focus on their bidirectional interactions with classic AD pathology (the ferroptosis hypothesis is relatively mature, while emerging hypotheses such as cuproptosis have not been fully elucidated). Metal homeostasis dysregulation can directly promote β-amyloid aggregation, tau hyperphosphorylation, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and regulated cell death. Conversely, these pathological processes can also alter the binding, storage, transport, and subcellular distribution of metal ions. Dysregulated metal ions function as "context-dependent" modulators of pathological processes. Their functional effects depend on metal species, concentration, binding state, subcellular compartment, and disease stage. Metal homeostasis dysregulation associated with AD may essentially reflect a redistribution between physiological and pathological pools. Ideal interventions should selectively neutralize pathological metal pools while preserving or restoring essential metal-dependent neuronal functions. By integrating the latest advances in the field of metal-targeted therapies (chelators, metabolic modulators, biomarkers, metal imaging, and gene editing), we emphasize that future treatments should shift from nonspecific metal clearance toward precise metal regulation and precision medicine.

articles.title: A Pilot Randomized Study of NAT2 and YEATS4 Pharmacogenetic Return of Results in Adults with Hypertension and African Ancestry: The GUARDD-US PGx Study.
articles.abstract: Almost half of individuals with hypertension fail to achieve recommended blood pressure (BP) goals. Pharmacogenetic gene-drug interactions may alter the efficacy of antihypertensive agents. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled sub-study of participants (N = 1874) with hypertension and self-reported African ancestry to determine whether pharmacogenetic return of results (RoR) would improve systolic blood pressure (SBP) at 3 months. Participants were randomized to immediate pharmacogenetic RoR (intervention) or delayed RoR at trial completion (control). Clinical decision support conveyed recommendations for YEATS4-guided thiazide diuretic selection and NAT2-guided hydralazine dosing. Prespecified subgroup analyses included those with uncontrolled BP (baseline SBP ≥140 or DBP ≥90 mm Hg) and actionable genotypes. Immediate RoR did not improve SBP at 3 months in a broad population of hypertensive adults with controlled and uncontrolled SBP (covariate-adjusted change in SBP between groups: -0.3 ± 0.74 mm Hg, 95% CI: -1.8, 1.2). In participants with an actionable YEATS4 genotype (N = 867) predicting reduced thiazide efficacy, immediate RoR led to greater SBP reduction at 3 months (-2.46 mm Hg, 95% CI: -4.57 to -0.36). In participants with uncontrolled hypertension at baseline (N = 659), immediate RoR led to a greater reduction in SBP (-2.9 ± 0.74 mm Hg, 95% CI: -5.6, -0.3). Although no SBP reduction was observed in the whole cohort, participants with an actionable YEATS4 genotype or uncontrolled BP who received immediate RoR had a significantly greater SBP improvement than those with delayed RoR. Future studies of antihypertensive pharmacogenetics should recruit individuals with uncontrolled BP and actionable genotypes.

articles.title: Alpha-ketoglutarate ameliorates systemic sclerosis-associated fibrosis by restoring endothelial function.
articles.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a devastating autoimmune disease characterized by multi-organ fibrosis with limited therapeutic options. Using targeted metabolomics, we first observed that levels of alpha-ketoglutarate (α-KG), a key TCA-cycle intermediate, were paradoxically elevated in bleomycin-induced fibrotic lungs and in TGF-β-stimulated fibroblasts, prompting us to test whether exogenous supplementation could augment this compensatory response. Using bleomycin-induced skin and lung fibrosis mouse models, we demonstrated that oral α-KG administration significantly attenuated dermal and pulmonary collagen deposition, reduced inflammatory infiltration, and improved survival. Although fibroblasts are conventionally regarded as the central effectors of fibrosis, integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk transcriptomic deconvolution unexpectedly identified endothelial cells as the predominant cellular target of α-KG in fibrotic lungs. Consistently, α-KG restored endothelial cell proportions in vivo, rescued angiogenic function and preserved barrier integrity in association with upregulation of eNOS, and tight junction proteins in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) treated with bleomycin. Mechanistically, α-KG suppressed TGF-β/Smad activation and reversed bleomycin-induced metabolic repression, including restoration of fatty acid oxidation signatures and mitochondrial ultrastructure, accompanied by upregulation of the mitochondrial biogenesis regulator NRF1. Collectively, these findings reveal that α-KG exerts broad anti-fibrotic effects in SSc models by protecting endothelial function and inhibiting canonical pro-fibrotic signaling, highlighting its potential as a translatable metabolic therapeutic strategy for SSc.

articles.title: Nifedipine-modulated gut microbiota attenuates hypertensive vascular injury through Bifidobacterium-associated inosine-Adora2b signaling.
articles.abstract: Although antihypertensive drugs mitigate hypertensive vascular injury, their vascular benefits are not fully explained by blood pressure reduction alone. Many cardiovascular drugs reshape the gut microbiota, which in turn influences their vascular pharmacology. We therefore investigated whether gut microbiota remodeling contributes to nifedipine-mediated vascular protection in high-salt hypertensive rats and a pilot patient cohort. Combining 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, fecal microbiota transplantation, microbiota depletion, supplementation, and selective receptor antagonism, we found that nifedipine ameliorated gut dysbiosis. Transplantation of nifedipine-modulated microbiota improved intestinal barrier integrity and reduced vascular inflammation, oxidative stress, collagen deposition, and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching, while only marginally lowering blood pressure. Conversely, microbiota depletion markedly attenuated these vascular benefits despite preserving nifedipine-induced blood pressure lowering. These vascular benefits were associated with nifedipine-restored Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis 420 (B420) and increased inosine availability. Supplementation with either recapitulated major vascular protective effects of nifedipine without statistically significant changes in blood pressure. In hypertensive patients, nifedipine treatment was associated with higher intestinal B420 abundance and inosine levels. In vitro, inosine modulated macrophages in an Adora2b- and Rap1-dependent manner, with accompanying changes in cAMP and KLF4, ameliorating VSMC dysfunction via paracrine signaling. In vivo, systemic Adora2b antagonism attenuated the vascular protective effects of both inosine and B420. Together, our findings support a gut microbiota-dependent component of nifedipine-mediated vascular protection that extends beyond blood pressure lowering, involving B420, increased inosine availability, and Adora2b signaling. We also nominate B420 and inosine as candidate adjuncts to calcium channel blocker therapy.

articles.title: Emerging therapeutic role of cinnamic acid derivatives in hyperuricemia and gout: mechanistic, translational, and pharmacological perspectives.
articles.abstract: Hyperuricemia and gout are increasingly common metabolic and inflammatory disorders characterized by excessive accumulation of uric acid, impaired urate excretion, oxidative stress, and monosodium urate crystal inflammation. Although currently available therapies such as xanthine oxidase inhibitors and uricosuric agents effectively reduce serum levels of uric acid, their long-term clinical use is often associated with adverse reactions, limited tolerability, and incomplete disease management. As a result, there is increasing interest in identifying natural compounds that may serve as a potential preclinical lead for the development of more targeted urate-lowering strategies. Cinnamic acid derivatives, including p-coumaric acid, caffeic acid, ferulic acid, sinapic acid, chlorogenic acid, and synthetic analogs such as 4-nitrocinnamic acid, have shown promising anti-hyperuricemic and anti-gout activities in experimental studies. These compounds have pharmacological effects through several mechanisms, including the inhibition of xanthine oxidase; modulation of urate transporters such as URAT1, GLUT9, and ABCG2; suppression of inflammatory pathways including NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome signalling; antioxidant activity; and protection against renal injuries induced by uric acid. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms, pharmacological evidence, and structure-activity relationships of selected cinnamic acid derivatives related to hyperuricemia and gout management. In addition, it discusses translational challenges associated with bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, toxicity evaluation, and clinical validation. Collectively, cinnamic acid derivatives represent promising pre-clinical leads that warrant further preclinical and clinical investigations to develop safer and more effective therapies against hyperuricemia and gout.

articles.title: Respiratory drug delivery: physiological, technical, and regulatory considerations for dissolution testing of orally inhaled dry powder aerosols.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pharmaceutical development of dry powder inhaler (DPI) products has traditionally relied on aerodynamic performance metrics. However, these parameters do not capture the post-deposition fate of inhaled particles, where dissolution impacts mucociliary clearance, macrophage uptake, retention and systemic absorption, particularly for poorly soluble drugs. Consequently, there is increasing interest in understanding the dissolution behavior of orally inhaled drug products. AREAS COVERED: This review critically examines the unique physiological environment of the lungs and the interactions of inhaled drugs with surfactants and mucins, highlighting why the respiratory tract cannot be regarded as a miniaturized gastrointestinal tract. It also discusses the dynamic interplay between dissolution and pulmonary clearance, alongside key methodological challenges in dissolution testing, including sample collection, apparatus design, dissolution media, and data analysis. Literature published between 1968 and 2026 was identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar and Web of Science databases. EXPERT OPINION: Widespread implementation of dissolution testing is hindered by the lack of standardized methodologies on aerosol collection, dissolution apparatuses, hydrodynamic conditions, and physiologically relevant dissolution media that can accurately replicate the lung environment. Future progress will require harmonized regulatory guidance, validated testing platforms for routine quality control and advanced biorelevant airway models for in vitro-in vivo relationship.

articles.title: Context-dependent protective and pathogenic functions of YTHDF1 in MASLD and hepatocellular carcinoma: Mechanisms and design of therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease and can progressively develop into inflammatory metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver fibrosis. During this progression, activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) leads to excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix. There is a growing trend to develop into hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The limited availability of effective therapeutics highlights the need to better understand the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is a key post-transcriptional RNA modification that regulates gene expression and governs a broad range of physiological and pathological processes. YTH domain family 1 (YTHDF1) is a reader protein that recognizes m6A modifications on mRNAs and enhances their stability or translation by interacting with key components of the translation machinery. YTHDF1 exhibits context-dependent functions in MASLD and liver fibrosis, while it promotes HCC pathogenesis. Hepatocytic YTHDF1 alleviates MASLD by improving mitochondrial function, serving as a protective factor during its early stages. YTHDF1 in HSCs is important for initiating liver fibrosis, yet it also plays a crucial role in regulating HSC ferroptosis to counteract established fibrosis. Our structure-based analyses of YTHDF1 inhibitors reveal novel concepts, including inhibition of YTHDF1-induced condensates and direct degradation of YTHDF1 proteins by fullerene derivatives and metal-organic frameworks. YTHDF1 inhibitors serve as selective chemical probes for interrogating YTHDF1's cell type-specific functions in MASLD. They are also promising candidates for in vivo evaluation to treat MASLD and HCC and to prevent liver fibrosis at early stages.

articles.title: Citicoline in cardiovascular protection: mechanistic roles of choline and acetylcholine.
articles.abstract: Citicoline (CDP-choline) is a rate-limiting precursor for phosphatidylcholine synthesis and acetylcholine production, and thus a unique metabolic hub linking membrane phospholipid homeostasis with cholinergic signaling. The biochemical rationale for the therapeutic potential of citicoline in heart disease is rooted in fundamental metabolic principles and conserved cytoprotective pathways. However, the cardiovascular evidence base for citicoline is not as extensive as its established neuroprotective profile. The cardioprotection is mainly mediated by the cholinergic system, including vagal efferent activity and the non-neuronal cardiac cholinergic system (NNCCS). This initiates a wide signaling network including PI3K/AKT, JAK/STAT, SIRT3/AMPK, IP3/calcium and MAPK cascades that inhibit inflammation, oxidative stress and apoptosis. Moreover, cholinergic signaling modulates proteasomal activity and microRNA expression, as well as post-transcriptional gene regulation to provide cardioprotection. This review summarizes experimental and clinical evidence in support of this hypothesis with particular emphasis on citicoline-activated mechanisms that are directly relevant for myocardial protection. These include phospholipid replacement of damaged sarcolemmal membranes and pleiotropic actions such as activation of survival kinase activation, suppression of inflammatory mediators, attenuation of oxidative injury and preservation of mitochondrial bioenergetics. Based on these safety data, we recommend that citicoline should be tested in further translational studies as an adjunctive treatment during reperfusion following myocardial infarction. Its antiarrhythmic effects, cholinergic engagement, downstream signaling modulation and miRNA regulation should be specifically highlighted as these may help limit infarct size, prevent adverse remodeling and improve clinical outcome in ischemic heart disease.

articles.title: Tryptophan Metabolism in Heart Failure: Mechanisms, Biomarker Potential, and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a complex clinical syndrome characterized by progressive cardiac remodeling, metabolic dysregulation, and high morbidity and mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence suggests that metabolic reprogramming plays a central role in HF progression, among which tryptophan (TRP) metabolism has attracted increasing attention due to its involvement in inflammation, immune regulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and gut microbiota imbalance. TRP is mainly metabolized through the kynurenine pathway (KP), serotonin pathway, and gut microbiota-derived indole pathway, generating a series of bioactive metabolites with distinct cardiovascular effects. Recent studies have demonstrated that abnormal activation of the indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO)-driven KP contributes to HF progression by promoting inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, myocardial fibrosis, and ventricular remodeling. In parallel, gut microbiota-derived TRP metabolites participate in the gut-heart axis and influence mitochondrial function, immune homeostasis, and cardiometabolic remodeling. In addition, TRP-related metabolites, particularly kynurenine (KYN) and the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio (KTR), exhibit promising potential as biomarkers for HF severity assessment and prognostic stratification. This review systematically summarizes the activation characteristics of TRP metabolic pathways in HF and discusses their mechanistic involvement in inflammation, immune regulation, gut microbiota dysbiosis, myocardial injury, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Furthermore, emerging therapeutic strategies targeting TRP metabolism are highlighted, including pharmacological modulation, microbiota-targeted interventions, exogenous metabolite supplementation, and exercise-based metabolic regulation. Collectively, TRP metabolism represents a promising metabolic hub integrating immune, inflammatory, and mitochondrial signaling networks in HF and may provide novel opportunities for precision diagnosis and targeted therapy.

articles.title: From metabolic starvation to precision therapy: engineering amino acid-targeted tumor therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Amino acid metabolism has emerged as a critical nexus linking tumor cell nutrient acquisition with immune microenvironmental regulation, providing a rich source of druggable targets for cancer therapy. Tumor cells engage in fierce metabolic competition with immune cells for key amino acids, including glutamine, arginine, tryptophan, and methionine, thereby establishing an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Over the past decade, therapeutic strategies targeting this metabolic axis have evolved from preclinical proof-of-concept to active clinical development across multiple biotechnology modalities. This review provides a comprehensive overview of amino acid metabolism-targeted therapeutics, emphasizing drug development trajectories and clinical translation prospects. Enzymatic depletion strategies, tumor-selective prodrugs and the clinical development landscape of small-molecule metabolic modulators are analyzed for tumor precision therapy. Despite promising efficacy, clinical translation faces challenges including compensatory metabolic resistance, patient stratification, and the immunosuppressive dichotomy of systemic amino acid depletion. The rational integration of metabolic modulation with immune checkpoint inhibition, chemotherapy, and precision delivery systems holds promise for advancing these therapies into standard oncological practice.

articles.title: The gastrointestinal KATP-ERK signaling axis: Molecular mechanisms, pharmacological opportunities, and emerging translational technologies.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: ATP-sensitive potassium channels are metabolic sensors that couple intracellular nucleotide availability to membrane excitability, calcium signaling, mitochondrial function, and cell survival. Growing evidence identifies KATP channels as essential regulators of gastrointestinal physiology. They are expressed in smooth muscle, enteric neurons, interstitial cells of Cajal, epithelial and enteroendocrine cells, microvascular cells, pericytes, and liver, where they contribute to motility, secretion, barrier integrity, nutrient sensing, vascular regulation, and mucosal protection. In parallel, ERK1/2 are central effectors of the MAPK pathway, controlling epithelial renewal, inflammation, fibrosis, apoptosis, and tissue repair. This review proposes an integrated KATP-ERK signaling network that regulates gastrointestinal homeostasis. METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched for relevant studies using combinations of the terms "ERK" AND "KATP channels" AND "cardiovascular" OR "gastrointestinal". RESULTS: Evidence supports functional crosstalk between KATP channels and ERK signaling. In this framework, KATP channels act as metabolic rheostats, whereas ERK integrates redox, growth factor, and stress-related signals. Acute KATP activation promotes adaptation by preserving mitochondrial function and epithelial barrier integrity, whereas chronic channel overactivation, as observed in Cantú syndrome caused by gain-of-function mutations in ABCC9 or KCNJ8, may induce maladaptive remodeling, tight junction disruption, apoptosis, fibrosis, and dysmotility. The potential involvement of FGFR/Klotho signaling as an upstream ERK regulator, together with KATP/ERK pharmacological modulation, FGF/Klotho-based therapies, and biosensor technologies for pathway monitoring in organoids and gut-on-chip models, is also discussed. CONCLUSIONS: The KATP-ERK-FGFR/Klotho framework links ion-channel pharmacology with gastrointestinal biology, providing a foundation for biomarker discovery, therapeutic development, and precision medicine approaches in gastrointestinal disorders.

articles.title: Gastrodin alleviates acute colitis with comorbid anxiety- and depression-like behaviours rather than cognitive dysfunction by modulating gut microbiota and suppressing inflammation.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients frequently suffer from emotional disturbances, predominantly anxiety- and depression-like symptoms, and may also have cognitive dysfunction, but the mechanisms remain unclear, and no therapies targeting the gut or nervous system exist. Gastrodin (GAS), the primary active component of Gastrodia elata, has anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects. Whether GAS can alleviate acute colitis with comorbid anxiety- and depression-like behaviours or cognitive dysfunction via the gut-brain axis is unknown. Using a 3% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse model, we administered GAS (240 mg/kg) by gavage for 7 days. The open field, elevated plus maze, tail suspension, and forced swimming tests showed that GAS improved behavioural abnormalities (including anxiety- and depression-like behaviours); it also restored colon length and reduced colonic histopathological injury. Metagenomic sequencing revealed that GAS reshaped the gut microbiota, increasing Sporosarcina and Nitrospirae while decreasing Clostridiaceae and Lachnospiraceae. Untargeted metabolomics indicated that GAS shifted the metabolic profile away from DSS and normalized taurine levels, and KEGG pathway analysis suggested that GAS may partially ameliorate DSS-induced metabolic disturbances by downregulating virulence-related pathways and upregulating energy metabolic pathways such as the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation relative to DSS. Western blot confirmed that GAS restored the tight junction protein Occludin and decreased TNF-α. Quantitative proteomics demonstrated that GAS reversed the aberrant expression of 191 colonic proteins. These results demonstrate correlative associations between GAS treatment and the alleviation of acute colitis and behavioural abnormalities, alongside concurrent changes in gut microbiota composition, metabolite profiles, and intestinal barrier proteins. Whether these associations reflect a causal gut-brain axis mechanism requires direct experimental validation. GAS modulates the microbiota, partially restores metabolism, repairs the gut barrier, and suppresses local inflammation, suggesting a potential gut-brain axis mechanism. These findings position GAS as a promising candidate for further mechanistic and translational investigation in IBD-associated behavioural comorbidities.

articles.title: Melatonin nanoemulgel for dermal applications: from formulation to in vivo imaging validation.
articles.abstract: Radiation-induced dermatitis is a prevalent side effect of radiotherapy worldwide. Conventional treatment strategies often fall short of achieving optimal therapeutic efficacy, primarily due to inadequate retention on the skin surface. This limitation has motivated research to find new nanotechnology-based treatment approaches to enhance therapeutic outcomes. Nanoformulations have emerged as a promising solution, offering improved therapeutic outcomes. In this study, authors investigated a combination therapy consisting of melatonin (MLT), vitamin E (VE), and N-acetyl cysteine (NAC). MLT is a naturally occurring hormone that has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that may help treat cancer. It plays a crucial part in protecting healthy tissues by neutralizing various free radical scavengers generated by IR pro-oxidant enzymes that are triggered after exposure to IR. VE and NAC also depict radiomitigator properties. In the present study, nanoemulgel was formulated with Carbopol®940, which acts as a gelatinizing agent to facilitate effective delivery of these therapeutic agents at the target site. Pseudoternary phase diagrams were prepared to classify the area of nanoemulsion region. Globule size and zeta potential of optimized nanoemulsion formulation were observed to be 113.84 ± 0.648 nm and 34.2 ± 0.907 mV, respectively. Further, in vitro skin release studies showed 49.94 ± 3.01% cumulative release of MLT from nanoemulgel a time frame of 24 h. And the formulation followed Korsmeyer-Peppas model, which indicates that drug release is non-fickian. An FTIR analysis confirmed that MLT's characteristic peaks were preserved in the formulations, demonstrating that no interaction occurred between the constituents. The DSC thermogram of MLT nanoemulgel showed no sharp melting peak, suggesting molecular dispersion in oil phase. Additionally, gamma scintigraphy evaluation confirmed the formulation's long-term skin retention. In experimental results, nanoemulsion gel showed enhanced permeability and retention, making it a promising transporter for topical deliveries of bioactives for radiation-induced dermatitis prevention.

articles.title: Evaluation of antiseptic drug candidate pyridosept in preclinical in vivo toxicity studies.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study is to assess the safety profile of the antiseptic drug candidate pyridosept in preclinical in vivo toxicity tests. The safety of pyridosept was assessed in acute toxicity tests in rats, mice and rabbits via dermal, intragastric, intraperitoneal, and inhalation routes of administration. Subchronic dermal toxicity of pyridosept was evaluated following cutaneous application for 90 days in rats and rabbits. Pyridosept was also examined in the accumulation test in rats and in micronucleus assay in the skin and bone marrow of mice after single and repeated administration. Acute oral toxicity study of pyridosept revealed an LD50 of 1208 mg/kg in mice and 1242 mg/kg in rats, a dermal LD50 > 2000 mg/kg in both species, and an LD50 of 23-32 mg/kg upon intraperitoneal administration. In the 90-day dermal toxicity study in rats, no systemic toxicity was found; the only treatment-related effects were reversible local skin reactions at intermediate and high doses. In the 90-day rabbit study, dermatitis, granulomatous hepatitis, and mild interstitial nephritis occurred; however, the incidence of hepatitis did not differ significantly from the control and showed no dose dependence. In the skin accumulation study, the cumulation coefficient (Kk = 12.8) indicated no cumulative properties, and the micronucleus assay demonstrated no mutagenic activity in mouse skin or bone marrow. Pyridosept's acute toxicity upon oral administration is more favorable than that of benzalkonium chloride, comparable to miramistin, and slightly less favorable than chlorhexidine. The results of in vivo pharmacokinetic, allergenic, and immunotoxicity studies of pyridosept will be presented in forthcoming publications.

articles.title: Investigation of the pharmacological and circuit basis for psychedelic drug effects on interval timing in mice.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Classical psychedelic drugs such as the tryptamine psilocybin can alter temporal perception. Previously, the phenylethylamine psychedelic 2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine (DOI), a 5-HT2A receptor agonist, altered timing precision and accuracy in mice performing the discrete-trials temporal discrimination task (TDT), a retrospective timing task where subjects differentially respond depending on whether a light is illuminated for shorter or longer than 6.5 s. OBJECTIVES: Although DOI alters TDT performance, it is unclear whether timing is altered by tryptamine psychedelics, which are less selective for 5-HT2 subtypes and also activate the 5-HT1A receptor. METHODS: To address this knowledge gap, we tested psilocin (the active metabolite of psilocybin) in male C57BL/6J mice performing the TDT and assessed the involvement of 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A receptors in its effects. Because the prefrontal cortex (PFC) is involved in psychedelic drug effects and temporal perception, additional experiments tested whether DOI microinfusion into the medial PFC (mPFC) replicates its systemic effects. RESULTS: Psilocin (0.8 mg/kg SC) altered timing accuracy and precision in mice performing the TDT, similarly to DOI. Psilocin effects were blocked by the 5-HT2A antagonist M100907 but were unaffected by the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY-100,635. Infusion of DOI bilaterally into mPFC mimicked the effect of systemic administration on TDT performance. Administration of the selective 5-HT2A inverse agonists M100907 and MDL 11,939 altered timing accuracy, demonstrating that both increases and reductions in 5-HT2A receptor activation can modulate perceived clock speed. CONCLUSIONS: The mPFC appears to play a role in TDT performance and may mediate the effects of psychedelic drugs on interval timing.

articles.title: Electrospun-lyophilized chitosan wound dressings for dual bioactive delivery of hyaluronic acid and IL-6.
articles.abstract: Wound healing is a complex and highly regulated cellular process with limited therapeutic interventions despite its substantial clinical burden. Current research shifts towards endogenous biomolecules as promising wound healing candidates, including hyaluronic acid and interleukin-6. However, despite their clinical potential such molecules pose significant technological challenges due to their fragility, limiting their clinical application. To overcome these limitations, a bilayer wound dressing was developed combining electrospinning and freeze drying. A chitosan nanofiber mat serves as a physical barrier, while hyaluronic acid and interleukin-6 were transformed into a hydrophilic wound-healing-promoting layer via freeze drying, enabling immediate and wound-phase-specific delivery of interleukin-6. Hyaluronic acid acts as a stabilizer for interleukin-6, enhancing its recovery by about 30 % and initial storage stability. The wound dressing demonstrates high biocompatibility, with a cell viability of 126 % and reduces the residual wound area and accelerates wound closure by more than 40 % after 48 h compared to the control. Further, pronounced antibacterial activity of chitosan is proven against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, further enhanced by hyaluronic acid through increased protonation of amino groups. These results provide proof-of-concept for the potential of this bilayer system as a multifunctional platform for the stable and effective delivery of fragile biomolecules enabling modern wound therapy.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Compound K Inhibits Complement C1qA/C3-CR3-Mediated Microglial Synaptic Pruning and Neuronal Pyroptosis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ginseng (Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer), a classic traditional Chinese medicine, has long been used for "calming the mind and enhancing intelligence" to combat cognitive decline. Its major metabolite, ginsenoside compound K (CK), exerts neuroprotection, but the molecular mechanisms against Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigated the molecular mechanism by which CK attenuates microglial aberrant synaptic phagocytosis and neuronal pyroptosis via inhibiting the complement C1qA cascade. MATERIALS AND METHODS: APP/PS1 mice were used as AD models and treated with CK (20 or 40 mg/kg/d) or memantine (MH, 3 mg/kg/d) by gavage once daily for 14 weeks. Morris water maze and open field tests were used to assess cognitive function and anxiety-like behavior, respectively. HE, Nissl and Golgi staining detected neuronal damage and synaptic integrity. Immunofluorescence and ELISA measured microglial polarization, activation and synaptic phagocytosis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations analyzed the CK-C1qA interaction. Western blot, immunofluorescence and ELISA detected complement components (C1qA, C3, CR3) and pyroptosis-related proteins (NF-κB, NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, GSDMD-N, IL-18). In vitro cellular experiments, including BV2 cell monoculture and BV2-HT22 transwell co-culture systems, were further performed to validate the causal role of C1qA. RESULTS: CK improved cognitive and anxiety behaviors in APP/PS1 mice, attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage, increased Nissl-positive neurons, restored dendritic complexity and spine density, and upregulated PSD95 and SYP. CK induced microglial M1-like-to-M2-like polarization and reduced Iba1+/CD68+ microglia colocalization with PSD95+ synapses, indicating suppressed synaptic engulfment. CK was predicted to bind to the C1qA globular head domain, reduced C1qA deposition at synapses, inhibited C3, and CR3 expression, suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation, downregulated NLRP3, ASC, cleaved-caspase-1, and GSDMD-N, decreased IL-18 release, and alleviated neuronal pyroptosis. In vitro, CK suppressed C1qA expression in BV2 cells and reduced synaptic C1qA deposition in HT22 cells. CONCLUSION: CK ameliorated cognitive and synaptic deficits in APP/PS1 mice by inhibiting the C1qA/C3-CR3 pathway to suppress aberrant microglial synaptic phagocytosis and blocking NF-κB/NLRP3/GSDMD-mediated neuronal pyroptosis. These findings elucidate CK's neuroprotective mechanisms and provide scientific evidence for ginseng's traditional cognitive benefits.

articles.title: IVIS assessment of mRNA-LNP protein expression: effects of dosing parameters and prior LNP exposure.
articles.abstract: Bioluminescence imaging using in vivo imaging systems (IVIS) is widely used to assess reporter protein expression after administration of messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). However, methodological variation and prior LNP exposure can complicate interpretation. Here, we evaluated selected parameters affecting IVIS readouts after intramuscular administration of firefly luciferase mRNA formulated in SM-102 or ALC-0315 LNPs in BALB/c mice. We also investigated the effects of repeated administration. D-luciferin delivery, imaging interval and mouse position influenced signal acquisition, while mRNA dose and injection volume affected the magnitude and regional distribution of expression. Background bioluminescence in mice receiving PBS was negligible compared with mRNA-LNP-associated signals, suggesting that dedicated negative-control groups may be unnecessary once baseline signal is established under consistent imaging conditions. Repeated administration of either SM-102 or ALC-0315 LNPs reduced expression following a subsequent mRNA-LNP dose. This occurred after prior administration of LNPs containing either firefly luciferase mRNA or non-coding polyadenylic acid, whereas repeated PBS injections had no comparable effect. Therefore, the reduced expression was associated with prior exposure to the LNP carrier rather than repeated injection or expression of the encoded reporter. These results highlight the need to standardise IVIS acquisition and dosing parameters, including mRNA dose, injection volume, and administration schedule, and demonstrate that prior LNP exposure can attenuate subsequent mRNA-mediated protein expression.

articles.title: Genistein targets Wnt5a to alleviate temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis by suppressing JNK/JUN-dependent MMP9 activation.
articles.abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage destruction, extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation, and chronic inflammation, yet effective disease-modifying therapeutic targets and pharmacological interventions remain limited. Using a monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced rat TMJ-OA model and interleukin-1β (IL-1β)-stimulated chondrocytes, we integrated transcriptomic analysis, chromatin accessibility profiling, and molecular screening to elucidate disease mechanisms and identify candidate compounds. Integrated RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis revealed Wnt family member 5a (Wnt5a) as a critical upstream regulator significantly associated with TMJ-OA progression, while assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) uncovered an inflammatory chromatin landscape characterized by enhanced activator protein-1 (AP-1) activity and JUN-dependent transcriptional regulation ofmatrix metalloproteinase 9 (Mmp9). Mechanistically, Wnt5a activated c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) signaling to promote JUN nuclear accumulation and enhance AP-1-mediatedMmp9transcription, leading to ECM degradation and chondrocyte dysfunction. Structure-based virtual screening and biophysical assays, including surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), identified genistein (GEN) as a small-molecule compound capable of directly binding Wnt5a, supported by cellular target-engagement evidence. Functionally, genistein suppressed the Wnt5a/JNK/JUN/MMP9 signaling axis, partially restored type II collagen (COL2A1) expression, alleviated oxidative stress, and preserved cartilage integrity in TMJ-OA rats. Collectively, these findings establish Wnt5a as a therapeutically actionable driver of TMJ-OA progression and identify genistein as a Wnt5a-targeting compound with cartilage-protective activity, providing a mechanism-based rationale for developing disease-modifying interventions for degenerative joint diseases.

articles.title: Metabolism-mediated herb-drug interaction between milk thistle and resmetirom in MCD diet-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis rat model.
articles.abstract: Resmetirom is a liver-directed thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, whereas milk thistle is widely used as a hepatoprotective supplement. This study evaluated whether milk thistle supplement coadministration alters resmetirom metabolism, systemic exposure, and pharmacological response. A validated LC-MS/MS method was used to quantify resmetirom in rat plasma and microsomal samples. Male Sprague-Dawley rats with a methionine and choline-deficient diet-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) received vehicle, resmetirom (8 mg/kg), milk thistle supplement (100 mg/kg total silybin A + B equivalent), or their combination for 8 days. Milk thistle increased resmetirom Cmax by 17 %, AUC0-t by 37 %, and AUC0-∞ by 32 %, while reducing apparent oral clearance by 25 %. In rat liver microsomes, milk thistle supplement extract (50 µM total silybin A + B equivalent) decreased the resmetirom elimination-rate constant from 0.0021 to 0.0002 min-1, prolonged microsomal half-life from 330.84 to 3914.31 min, and reduced intrinsic clearance from 3.88 to 0.39 µL/min/mg protein. The combination was associated with greater improvements in liver enzymes, bilirubin, lipid parameters, relative liver weight, body-weight recovery, and hepatic histology than either monotherapy. These findings provide preclinical evidence of a metabolism-mediated milk thistle-resmetirom interaction that increases resmetirom exposure and is accompanied by an enhanced pharmacodynamic response in rats.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin alleviates CYH33-induced hyperglycemia and preserves antitumor immunity against ovarian cancer in type 1 diabetic mice.
articles.abstract: PI3K is frequently hyperactivated in ovarian cancer and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target. CYH33 is a novel PI3Kα-selective inhibitor that has been approved in Japan for the treatment of ovarian clear cell carcinoma harboring PIK3CA mutations. However, its on-target adverse effect of hyperglycemia limits its clinical application, particularly in patients susceptible to diabetes, underscoring the urgent need to optimize therapeutic strategies to improve both safety and efficacy. In this study, we employed an ID8 syngeneic murine ovarian cancer model and demonstrated that CYH33 significantly inhibited tumor growth with a modest effect on glucose homeostasis. We then established mouse models of type 1 (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) to expose hyperglycemia induced by PI3K inhibition and identified that dapagliflozin effectively alleviated CYH33-induced hyperglycemia while preserving its antitumor activity in T1D mice. Mechanistically, the combination of CYH33 and dapagliflozin may improve the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in T1D mice, as evidenced by upregulation gene sets involved in interferon-α and interferon-γ response, as well as significantly enhanced infiltration of CD8+ T-cell in ID8 tumors. Furthermore, this combination synergized with anti-PD-1 antibody to further enhance antitumor efficacy. These findings provide a potential strategy for optimizing the clinical use of PI3K inhibitors and shed light on metabolic interventions to modulate tumor immune microenvironment.

articles.title: Amifostine attenuates pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and metabolic remodeling via the SIRT1/PPAR-α axis in rats.
articles.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy induced by chronic pressure overload is accompanied by significant metabolic disturbances, including impaired myocardial lipid metabolism. This study ascertained whether the cytoprotective agent amifostine (WR-2721) exerts cardioprotective effects along pressure overload-induced remodeling and whether these effects are linked to modulation of the SIRT1/PPAR-α axis. Male Wistar rats (n = 24) were assigned to Sham, abdominal aortic constriction (AAC), and AAC + amifostine (200 mg/kg, i.p., weekly for 8 weeks) groups, with amifostine administered concurrently with hypertrophic stress. The cardiac structure and function were appraised using echocardiography and histological analyses, with the expression of SIRT1, PPAR-α, and key regulators of lipid metabolism examined by Western blotting. Amifostine treatment was associated with attenuation of pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy, reflected by lower heart and lung weight ratios, preservation of functional indices, and diminished myocardial fibrosis. At the molecular level, amifostine administration was accompanied by relative normalization of SIRT1 and PPAR-α expression, elevated levels of fatty acid oxidation-related proteins, and suppression of lipogenic markers. These findings suggest that amifostine mitigates pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and is associated with improved myocardial metabolic homeostasis, accompanied by favorable changes in the expression of SIRT1, PPAR-α, and lipid metabolism-related proteins. While these observations support the potential involvement of the SIRT1/PPAR-α signaling pathway, further mechanistic studies are required to establish its causal role in mediating the cardioprotective effects of amifostine.

articles.title: Repurposing Entrectinib and Ibrutinib as MNK/eIF4E Pathway Modulators in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.abstract: The ERK/MNK/eIF4E signaling axis is critically involved in cap-dependent translation and significantly impacts survival and chemotherapy resistance in ovarian cancer. Clinical data indicate that elevated eIF4E expression is an independent prognostic marker for poor overall survival (HR=1.17, p=0.027). However, there has yet to be a systematic evaluation of FDA-approved agents for their efficacy as MNK/eIF4E inhibitors. In the present study, a total of 2,180 FDA-approved compounds were screened using a comprehensive approach integrating machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and binding free energy analysis to identify potential MNK1 modulators. Ibrutinib and Entrectinib emerged as the most promising candidates, forming stable complexes with MNK1 and displaying favorable binding energies (Entrectinib: ΔG = -131.66 ± 2.05 kJ/mol; Ibrutinib: ΔG = -87.36 ± 2.04 kJ/mol). Notably, Ibrutinib, conventionally recognized as a BTK inhibitor, and Entrectinib, a tropomyosin receptor kinase inhibitor, exhibited previously unreported off-target interactions with MNK1/eIF4E, suggesting new therapeutic applications for both agents. In vitro validation was conducted using the A2780-s and A2780-cp cell lines, with A2780-cp selected for its elevated MNK/eIF4E activity. Niclosamide, identified as an MNK/eIF4E inhibitor, served as a positive control in this investigation. Both compounds significantly diminished cell viability, lowered the p-eIF4E/eIF4E ratio as determined via Western blot analysis, impaired clonogenic survival, and induced S-phase arrest in A2780-cp cells. This study represents the first examination of the roles of Entrectinib and Ibrutinib as modulators of MNK1/eIF4E in ovarian cancer, providing substantial functional evidence for their efficacy in modulating the MNK/eIF4E pathway with eIF4E Phosphorylation-Suppressing Activity.

articles.title: Oxycodone self-administration induces microRNA and gene expression changes in the rat nucleus accumbens.
articles.abstract: Prescription opioid abuse remains a critical public health concern and is a major risk factor for the development of opioid use disorder (OUD). Thus, there is an urgent need to better understand the neurobiological mechanisms underlying OUD in order to develop therapeutics and address the ongoing opioid epidemic. In this study, we hypothesized that microRNAs regulate gene expression changes following oxycodone self-administration. To test our hypothesis, we utilized a long-access drug self-administration paradigm in rats. Briefly, adult male Sprague-Dawley rats were trained to self-administer oxycodone (0.15mg/kg/infusion) or saline and were sacrificed 24h (withdrawal) following the last self-administration session. Brains were collected and the nucleus accumbens (NAc) was extracted and was processed for small RNA and RNA sequencing. We found that oxycodone self-administration changed the expression of 40 genes and 16 mature microRNAs (miRNAs). Bioinformatic predictions revealed that opioid-regulated genes are predicted targets of differentially regulated miRNAs, suggesting that miRNAs contribute to opioid-mediated transcriptomic changes in the NAc. Furthermore, we validated some of these findings in an independent cohort of male and female rats and across different stages of the addiction cycle. We identified miRNAs that are dynamically regulated during oxycodone withdrawal, as well as others that exhibit sustained regulation across different stages of the addiction cycle. Taken together, our data show that miRNAs may contribute to opioid-regulated gene expression and point to the therapeutic potential of miRNAs for OUD.

articles.title: Glycyrrhizic acid alters [99mTc]Tc-PSMA biodistribution and tumour progression in a DMBA-induced breast cancer model.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer remains a major global health challenge, and understanding interactions between pharmacological agents and radiopharmaceuticals is important for interpreting molecular imaging findings. Glycyrrhizic acid (GA), a bioactive triterpenoid derived from Glycyrrhiza glabra, has reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities; however, its effects on PSMA-targeted radiotracer biodistribution remain poorly investigated. This study evaluated GA effects on tumour-related biological responses and [99mTc]Tc-PSMA biodistribution in vitro and in vivo. Cytotoxicity, migration, and invasion were assessed in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells. Cell-free PSMA enzyme kinetics and a separate cellular [99mTc]Tc-PSMA uptake assay were performed to distinguish effects on PSMA enzymatic activity from cell-associated radiotracer uptake. In vivo studies used a DMBA-induced mammary tumour model in female Sprague-Dawley rats, followed by SPECT/CT imaging and tissue biodistribution analysis. GA reduced cell viability concentration-dependently (IC₅₀ = 20 µM at 48 h) and suppressed migration and invasion. Cell-free kinetic analysis showed an apparent non-competitive PSMA inhibition pattern (Ki = 12.4 ± 1.5 µM), although this does not establish the molecular binding site. In vivo, GA reduced tumour uptake of [99mTc]Tc-PSMA by 57% (P < 0.005) and altered non-target tissue distribution. Despite reduced absolute tumour uptake, the tumour-to-background ratio increased because background activity decreased proportionally more. GA was also associated with reduced tumour growth and metastatic burden and altered inflammatory, angiogenic, and apoptotic markers. Overall, GA alters tumour biology and [99mTc]Tc-PSMA biodistribution, while the mechanism underlying radiotracer changes remains unresolved.

articles.title: Cholinergic-Dependent Metaplasticity in the Amygdala-Insula Pathway During Incubation of Cocaine Craving.
articles.abstract: The time-dependent increase in drug seeking during abstinence, termed 'incubation of craving' is believed to play a major role in the persistent risks of relapse. This phenomenon is associated with synaptic plasticity changes across brain structures involved in reward processing, executive functions, emotion regulation and inhibitory control. The basolateral amygdala (BLA) and the anterior insular cortex (aIC) are two interconnected structures involved in processing internal and external drug-related cues and are known to play a role in drug craving. However, whether chronic cocaine alters synaptic plasticity within the BLA-aIC circuit and how these changes evolve during abstinence remains unclear. Here, using cocaine self-administration and in vivo electrophysiological recordings in anesthetized male rats, we demonstrate that, while long-term potentiation in the BLA-aIC pathway remains intact, long-term depression is disrupted throughout abstinence in both cocaine- and sucrose-rats, indicating a persistent impairment in synaptic weakening mechanisms. Importantly, a loss of depotentiation was observed after late but not early abstinence, and was specific to cocaine self-administration, identifying it as a hallmark of incubation of craving. Systemic, but not local intra-aIC, blockade of muscarinic receptors with atropine restored depotentiation and reduced cocaine-seeking behavior. Finally, qPCR analysis revealed region-specific transcriptional adaptations, with upregulation of muscarinic, NMDA and AMPA receptor transcripts in the BLA and a selective decrease of Grin2a in the aIC. Together, these findings point to cholinergic regulation of BLA-aIC metaplasticity as a candidate mechanism underlying incubation of cocaine craving.

articles.title: Therapeutic Potential and Toxicological Trade-Offs of Nanoparticle-Enhanced Valproic Acid in Glioblastoma: Behavioral and Oxidative Insights.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model. METHODS: We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n=12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA. RESULTS: VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD. CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.

articles.title: Exploring the pharmacological mechanism of Sanfu Patch for prevention and treatment of asthma from chronopharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics based on "winter disease cured in summer".
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The Sanfu Patch (SFP) is applied to back acupoints on the hottest days in summer to treat asthma, a winter-prone disease, and has been used in China for thousands of years. However, chrono- and temperature-related properties of treating asthma and the transdermal properties of active components are not fully clarified. AIM OF STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the anti-asthmatic chronopharmacodynamics and transdermal pharmacokinetics of SFP based on the theory of "winter disease cured in summer". MATERIALS AND METHODS: Chrono- and temperature-dependent Balb/c mouse models of OVA-induced asthma were established. The lung histopathology, pulmonary function testing, ELISA assays and Western blotting experiments were used for evaluating anti-asthma effect of transdermal SFP. The anti-inflammatory effects of six bioactive compounds were evaluated in vitro using BEAS-2B cells. The CETSA and SPR technique were employed to investigate whether the active components of SFP bind to anti-asthmatic proteins. The transdermal properties of active ingredients were analyzed by in vivo microdialysis assays. RESULTS: Applying SFP on the back in summer can prevent the occurrence of asthma over a relatively long period of time. The preventive effect against asthma diminished progressively at one, three and five months after administration of SFP. Compared with SFP administration in low-temperature (17°C) environment, SFP transdermal administration in high-temperature (33°C) environment was demonstrated a more significant therapeutic effect in alleviating asthma symptoms, airway hyperresponsiveness, and airway inflammation. High-temperature administration of SFP further reduced the expression of CD40, CD40L, and CLN5 in asthmatic mice. Tetrahydropalmatine, allocryptopine, protopine, tetrahydrocoptisine, dehydrocorydaline, and sinapine thiocyanate were screened as key components contributing to the therapeutic effects of SFP against asthma, exhibiting in vitro anti-inflammatory effects. CETSA results showed that the thermal stability of CD40, CD40L and CLN5 was significantly enhanced after the treatment of the above six components. The direct SPR binding confirmed that protopine and sinapine thiocyanate could bind to the three target proteins. The AUC(0-t) and Cmax values of all six components were higher at 33°C than those at 17°C after transdermal administration of SFP. CONCLUSIONS: This study has demonstrated the temperature advantages of the SFP application method for relieving asthma from chronopharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic perspectives, providing a foundation for subsequent research and therapeutic applications.

articles.title: Deposition of inhaled aerosols in the human lung: From infancy to adulthood.
articles.abstract: This narrative review discusses the effects that healthy aging has on particle deposition in the lungs. The lung structure and its size, breathing patterns and minute ventilation are all affected by age, from infancy through adulthood. These age-dependent variations in turn affect total and regional deposition in the healthy lung. While, for age-specific breathing patterns, overall deposition of inhaled particles tends to be higher in children than in adults, regional deposition is age- and particle size-dependent. For aerosols in the 1-5 µm size range, typical of pharmaceutical aerosols, deposition fraction in the upper respiratory tract is higher in children (<15 year old) than in adults while the opposite is observed in the intrathoracic lungs where deposition fraction is lower in children than in adults. However, compared to adults, children have smaller lung surface area over which the deposited dose is distributed. Consequently, the deposition rate per lung surface area is higher in the intrathoracic lungs of children than of adults. In adulthood, aging appears to have little effect on overall deposition during tidal breathing. However, for deep aerosol inhalation, studies suggest an increased deposition in the lung periphery with aging due to airway closure occurring at higher lung volume in the elderly than in young adults. These observations suggest that both therapeutic aerosol delivery and the adverse effects of particle matter exposure may be altered with age through the lifespan.

articles.title: Nebulization-stable lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery in advanced in vitro respiratory models.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary delivery of messenger RNA (mRNA) offers a promising strategy for local vaccination and treating respiratory diseases, but aerosolization stress and airway barriers remain major obstacles. Here, we developed PEG-free lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles (mucLPs) composed of a solid polylactic acid (PLA) core and an engineered lipid corona. Nine formulations were screened by varying lipid composition and were evaluated for physicochemical properties, mRNA association, cytocompatibility, stability during vibrating-mesh nebulization, and transfection. The lead formulation, mucLP3, combined high mRNA association with a negative post-loading surface charge and preserved its size distribution and reporter activity after nebulization. By contrast, the SM-102-based reference LNP tested under the same conditions showed aggregation and reduced reporter expression after nebulization. Non-nebulized mucLP3 also supported mRNA expression in airway epithelial cell lines, mouse lung organoids, and primary human airway epithelial cultures maintained at an air-liquid interface. These data establish a proof of concept for a PEG-free lipid-polymer hybrid architecture that tolerates the tested nebulization procedure and remains functional in respiratory models of increasing complexity. Direct mucus-transport measurements, aerosol-deposition studies, and in vivo efficacy studies will be required to establish pulmonary delivery performance.

articles.title: Bola-amphiphilic dendrimers with tunable architecture for ROS-responsive precision delivery of doxorubicin.
articles.abstract: Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers capable of precise intracellular drug release are critical for improving the efficacy and safety of cancer chemotherapy. However, many existing systems suffer from limited structural tunability and incomplete integration of molecular architecture, self-assembly, and responsiveness, which constrains tumor delivery and therapeutic performance. Here, we report reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive bola-amphiphilic dendrimers with tunable dendron generations, bola4A and bola8A, as a platform for doxorubicin (DOX) delivery and systematic comparison. Both dendrimers displayed high drug-loading capacities and stable nanoassembly formation, whereas bola4A, with lower-generation PAMAM dendrons, permitted more efficient stimulus penetration into the nanosystems. This architectural feature enhanced ROS- and pH-triggered drug release, promoted cellular uptake, and accelerated endosomal escape. Importantly, modulation of dendron generation systematically altered nanoparticle architecture and responsiveness, directly dictating therapeutic efficacy. Consequently, bola4A/DOX nanoparticles achieved superior tumor accumulation and tissue penetration, together with improved anticancer efficacy in vitro and in ovarian cancer SKOV3 xenograft models and reduced systemic toxicity relative to free DOX. These results establish dendritic architecture as a key determinant of stimuli-responsiveness and drug delivery performance, and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation stimuli-responsive nanomedicines tailored to pathological microenvironments.

articles.title: Probiotic-loaded biomaterial for wound healing and tissue regeneration: a unique medical tool.
articles.abstract: Deeper skin wounds lead to infections prolonging the healing process resulting in further complications. Although the treatment protocol includes mostly the use of antibiotics, the main challenge comes with their resistance and poor pharmacokinetics. Selective strain specific probiotic infused hydrogel system is one such newer approach in wound management to counter these issues. The highly sensitive probiotic strain needs proper conditions for colonization and protection against external environment. In this study, an economically feasible and simple attempt was made to incorporate the probiotics into a polymeric composite. Locust bean gum and gum odina were allowed to form a polymeric mix, into which Lactobacillus rhamnosus MTCC 5897, a probiotic was incorporated using CaCl2 as the crosslinker. The probiotic bound composite films were assessed for their microstructure, swelling ability, probiotic stability along with probiotic viability. Additionally, the antioxidant, cytocompatibility and antibacterial properties of the film were investigated. Furthermore, the in vivo wound model on rats indicated satisfactory healing rate along with collagen deposition. Therefore, the results demonstrated preliminary findings of the film that may act as a wound healing tool which further would require several clinical trials to be accepted commercially, and also paves way for further future research on advanced biomaterials focused on living bacterial hydrogel film providing wound healing potency.

articles.title: Impact of oxidative degradation on the bioavailability of subcutaneously administered adalimumab.
articles.abstract: Subcutaneous (SC) administration of therapeutic antibodies enhances patient convenience and healthcare resource efficiency compared to intravenous (IV) delivery, but therapy can be limited by incomplete bioavailability (BA) of SC biotherapeutics. This limitation may be attributed to processes inherent to the unique composition of SC tissue, including the potential presence of reactive oxygen species (ROS) within the SC microenvironment, which can induce chemical and structural instability and functional impairment. This study investigated the impact of oxidation on the SC BA of adalimumab (Humira® biosimilar) as a representative IgG1 therapeutic protein. Two models of oxidation, mimicking some of those ROS encountered in the SC tissue, were applied to adalimumab, then the resulting oxidized variants were characterized and subsequently administered SC to rats to evaluate changes in SC BA. HPLC-MS/MS analysis identified methionine residues within CH2-CH3 interface as the primary sites of oxidation. Oxidation at these sites correlated with reduced conformational stability, alterations in the charge variant profile, and diminished binding affinity to the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn). SC administration of oxidized species at 18% (w/w), diluted with excess unstressed IgG, to rats resulted in a slight decrease in SC BA, although not statistically significant. Additionally, oxidized AdmAb showed prolonged retention at the SC injection site, which may be associated with reduced conformational stability and higher propensity to aggregation and precipitation, although the underlaying mechanism requires further studies. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that oxidation can substantially alter the biophysical stability and FcRn binding affinity, while administering a moderate proportion of those oxidized species 18% (w/w) results in minimal changes in PK profile and overall SC BA.

articles.title: Peripheral GALR2 activation by the metabolically stabilized spexin analog LIT-01-144 produces potent opioid‑independent antinociception.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain constitutes a major global health burden, and current management remains largely dependent on opioid analgesics, which are associated with opioid use disorder. Accordingly, there is a pressing need to identify non-opioid therapeutic strategies. Galanin receptors (GALR1-3) have been implicated in pain modulation, but their individual roles remain insufficiently defined because of the absence of subtype-selective ligands. Recently, spexin has been identified as an endogenous peptide that selectively activates GALR2 and GALR3, offering a new scaffold for developing pharmacological tools targeting these receptor subtypes. In this study, we designed and characterized LIT-01-144, a modified spexin analog incorporating N-terminal fluorocarbon functionalization to improve metabolic stability while preserving receptor selectivity. In vitro pharmacological profiling demonstrated high potency at GALR2 and GALR3, with negligible activity at GALR1. Pharmacokinetic analyses showed a substantially prolonged plasma half-life relative to native spexin and no evidence of central nervous system penetration. In vivo, intracerebroventricular administration of LIT-01-144 produced robust antinociception at doses tenfold lower than those required for spexin. Although systemic administration had no detectable effect in naïve mice, it significantly attenuated pain-related behaviors in a model of persistent inflammatory pain. This effect was mediated specifically by GALR2 and was independent of opioid receptor signaling. In situ hybridization further showed an increase in Galr2 + neurons in dorsal root ganglia of inflamed mice. Collectively, these findings highlight GALR2 as a promising peripheral target for developing non-opioid analgesics and demonstrate the potential of LIT-01-144 as a valuable tool for understanding GALR2-mediated mechanisms of pain modulation.

articles.title: Adolescent-onset regular cannabis use is associated with altered neural and behavioural responses during anticipation and feedback of monetary reward and loss.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Regular cannabis use has been associated with alterations in reward-related neural processes, yet findings remain inconsistent and the relationship between neural activity and behavioural performance is not fully understood. OBJECTIVES: The present study aimed to characterise neural and behavioural correlates of reward processing in regular cannabis users (CU) compared with matched non-users (NU) using the Monetary Incentive Delay Task (MIDT). METHODS: Twenty adolescent-onset regular cannabis users (CU; ≥4 days/week for 2 years, with regular use initiated before age 18) and twenty age- and sex-matched non-users (NU) completed the Monetary Incentive Delay Task during functional MRI. Firstly, we assessed behavioural performance through reaction times, accuracy and monetary earnings to determine whether potential neural alterations were reflected in task performance. Secondly, focusing on reward-related brain regions, we examined group differences in BOLD functional MRI activity during anticipation and outcome phases separately for monetary win and loss conditions. Finally, we explored the association between behavioural performance and neural activation. RESULTS: Our findings provide preliminary evidence that adolescent-onset regular cannabis use is associated with altered engagement of key nodes within the mesocorticolimbic circuit accompanied by impaired behavioural performance. Particularly, compared with NU, CU showed (I) lower striatal activity during anticipation of monetary win and higher ventral striatum and frontal pole activity during anticipation of monetary loss; (II) different VTA BOLD contrast estimates during outcome of successful monetary win and loss avoidance, and lower frontal pole activity during outcome of unsuccessful loss avoidance; (III) lower monetary rewards and a trend towards slower reaction times and reduced accuracy; (IV) disrupted brain-behaviour coupling. CONCLUSIONS: Results from this study may help inform future research on the neurobiological mechanisms underlying changes in reward function and the resultant behavioural consequences of adolescent-onset cannabis use.

articles.title: Synthetic cannabinoid-induced changes in thalamo-prefrontal gamma synchrony and thalamic high-voltage spindles.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Cannabinoids, including Δ⁹-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and potent synthetic analogs, disrupt cognitive and perceptual processes via dysregulated neural oscillations. While these effects within limbic-cortical circuits have been well documented, the contribution of thalamocortical loops, which act as critical hubs for sensory gating and cognitive integration, remains unexplored. OBJECTIVES: To characterize the effects of acute synthetic cannabinoid exposure on thalamo-prefrontal oscillatory dynamics, specifically focusing on local gamma power, inter-regional synchrony, and cross-frequency coupling relevant. METHODS: We performed simultaneous local field potential (LFP) recordings from the mediodorsal thalamus (MD), prelimbic (PrL), and orbitofrontal (OFC) cortices in freely moving rats following acute administration of the potent synthetic cannabinoid 5F-EDMB-PICA (0.3 mg/kg, i.p.). RESULTS: 5F-EDMB-PICA significantly suppressed low- (30-49 Hz) and high-gamma (51-80 Hz) power in PrL and MD, with a transient low-gamma reduction in OFC, while increasing long-range gamma coherence between the MD and prefrontal regions in both sub-bands. Notably, the drug increased the occurrence of high‑voltage spindles (HVS, 6-12 Hz) recorded in the MD, and enhanced phase-amplitude coupling between the phase of both HVS and theta (4-8 Hz) and the amplitude of prefrontal gamma. CONCLUSIONS: These results reveal that acute synthetic cannabinoid exposure produces a dissociation between local and long-range oscillatory dynamics in the thalamo-prefrontal circuit, which possibly is driven by increased thalamic rhythmic output. This pattern of network reorganization may underlie cannabinoid-induced deficits in sensorimotor gating and cognitive integration.

articles.title: Beyond psychedelic exceptionalism: how people combine meditation with psychoactive substances, and how this relates to well-being.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Combining meditation with psychoactive substances is often assumed to be a niche practice centred on classic psychedelics. We sought to broaden this narrative in two cross-sectional studies. METHODS: Study 1 used a broad naturalistic sample (N = 1,391) to examine the prevalence of substance use, meditation, and their simultaneous combination, as well as associations with subjective happiness. Study 2 used a stratified subsample (n = 397) focusing on classic psychedelic and cannabis users, the most common psychedelic-type substances combined with meditation, to assess associations with mental well-being, peace of mind, psychological flexibility, depression, and anxiety. RESULTS: Contrary to prevailing assumptions, alcohol (29%), cannabis (19%), and nicotine (16%) were far more commonly combined with meditation than classic psychedelics (6%). Classic psychedelic use was also embedded within a pattern of pronounced polysubstance use, suggesting that it may reflect a broader substance-use profile rather than an isolated behavioural practice. Regression analyses found no consistent associations between psychedelic or cannabis use, with or without meditation, and any outcome. However, an unexpected pattern emerged for other drugs and alcohol. Other- drug use without meditation was associated with poorer well-being outcomes relative to no other-drug use, whereas other-drug use combined with meditation was not. Alcohol combined with meditation was associated with better well-being outcomes relative to alcohol use without meditation. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that combining meditation with substance use is not limited to psychedelics and should be studied within broader patterns of polysubstance use and meditation practice.

articles.title: What goes up must comedown: prevalence rates, characteristics, and coping strategies concerning MDMA aftereffects.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: MDMA is increasingly being studied for therapeutic applications, yet the prevalence and characteristics of post-acute negative effects remain debated. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize MDMA's post-acute negative effects, including prevalence and symptom profile among recreational users. Given preclinical work and limited human evidence suggesting that certain supplements and antidepressants may mitigate MDMA's negative effects, we also assessed the use of these substances as coping strategies. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of 497 MDMA-experienced participants recruited from Prolific. The survey assessed post-acute negative effects prevalence, timing, and duration; post-acute side effects; emotional changes, suicidal ideation; and intentional use of supplements or antidepressants to manage symptoms. We compared characteristics of post-acute side effects between MDMA users who self-reported ever experiencing a negative post-acute MDMA experience (colloquially known as a 'comedown') and those who did not. RESULTS: 74.5% of participants reported experiencing a period of post-acute negative effects at least once, with onset occurring approximately 24 hours post-ingestion and lasting an average of 40 hours. The most common symptoms were fatigue (88.1%), difficulty concentrating (85.7%), restlessness (82.9%), and headache (79.7%). 14.6% of post-acute negative effects experiencers endorsed passive suicidal ideation and 6.2% endorsed active suicidal ideation. Regarding coping strategies, 30.3% reported using supplements (most commonly N-acetyl-cysteine, acetyl-L-carnitine, and magnesium) and 5.1% reported using antidepressants, with moderate perceived helpfulness. CONCLUSIONS: Post-acute negative effects of MDMA appear prevalent among recreational users in a cross-sectional sample, characterized by fatigue, negative affect, and elevated suicidal ideation. These findings highlight post-acute risks that warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Serotonin 1B receptors expressed on forebrain excitatory neurons mediate the post-acute anxiolytic response to psilocybin in mice.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psilocybin can produce rapid and sustained antidepressant-like and anxiolytic effects, yet the receptor and circuit mechanisms underlying these behavioral changes remain unclear. While the serotonin 2A receptor mediates psilocybin's acute psychedelic effects, psilocin (the active metabolite of psilocybin) binds many serotonin receptor subtypes. Our prior work has identified the serotonin 1B receptor (5-HT1BR) as being necessary for the post-acute pro-hedonic and anxiolytic effects of psilocybin in mice. 5-HT1BRs are widely expressed throughout the brain on many different neuron subtypes. METHODS: In order to assess the role of 5-HT1BR expression on terminals of forebrain excitatory neurons in the response to psilocybin, we used a conditional genetic approach to selectively eliminate expression of htr1b in forebrain excitatory neurons using the Emx1 promoter. We examined acute behavioral responses, post-acute anxiolytic effects, and brain-wide neural activation to a single high dose of psilocybin in male and female mice. RESULTS: The absence of 5-HT1BR expression on Emx1+ neurons did not alter psilocybin's acute behavioral effects, including head twitch responding and hyperlocomotion. However, psilocybin's post-acute anxiolytic effects in the elevated plus maze (EPM) and novelty suppressed feeding (NSF) assays were strongly attenuated in mice lacking these receptors.
