Whole-brain c-Fos mapping across 190 regions revealed that psilocybin produced robust activation across the brain in both genotypes, including prefrontal cortices, corticolimbic structures, and sensory cortices. Network-level analyses revealed that psilocybin drove broad inter-regional decorrelation in control mice but increased synchronization in knockouts, with thalamic, prefrontal, and amygdala circuits most strongly affected. CONCLUSIONS: These findings implicate 5-HT1BRs expressed on terminals of forebrain excitatory neurons as a potential circuit-level excitatory gating mechanism. Overall, these receptors may be important for a coordinated network reorganization following psilocybin that contributes to the anxiolytic behavioral effects.

articles.title: Drug-Specific Associations of Angiotensin Receptor Blockers With Parkinson's Disease Risk in a Multicenter Electronic Health Record Cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) have demonstrated neuroprotective effects in preclinical models of Parkinson's disease (PD), but individual ARBs differ in pharmacological properties that may influence their neuroprotective potential. OBJECTIVES: Using large-scale hospital electronic health records of the University of California health system, we tested whether specific ARBs are associated with lower PD risk. METHODS: We conducted a new-user, active-comparator cohort study in the University of California Health Data Warehouse, encompassing 890 712 hypertensive patients across six academic medical centers from 2012 to 2025. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios for individual ARB associations with incident PD, adjusting for demographics, nine preindex comorbidities, and index date. Robustness was assessed through propensity score matching and negative-control analysis. RESULTS: Drug-specific Cox analysis identified irbesartan (HR = 0.588, 95% CI 0.434 to 0.796, p = 0.0006) and olmesartan (HR = 0.797, 95% CI 0.665 to 0.956, p = 0.015) as associated with lower PD risk. Irbesartan survived Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and propensity score matching supported both associations. CONCLUSION: In this large multicenter EHR cohort, irbesartan and olmesartan were associated with lower incident Parkinson's disease risk. These findings support further investigation of the renin-angiotensin system as a therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease and may inform the development or repurposing of agents with favorable central nervous system penetration and neuroprotective potential.

articles.title: Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD-), leucine-rich repeat (LRR-), and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome and snake venoms/toxins: mechanisms, pathophysiological relevance, and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: Snake envenoming triggers a complex inflammatory response that substantially contributes to local tissue destruction and systemic complications. Among the innate immune pathways implicated in venom-induced injury, the nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD-), leucine-rich repeat (LRR-), and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome has emerged as a key sensor-effector platform linking tissue damage, ionic imbalance, reactive oxygen species (ROS), lipid mediators, and cytokine maturation. Experimental studies indicate that crude venoms and isolated snake toxins, including Lys49 and Asp49 phospholipase A2 (PLA2), metalloproteinases, and C-type lectin/C-type lectin-like proteins, can activate NLRP3 inflammasome-dependent signaling, leading to caspase-1 activation, interleukin (IL)-1β release, and, in some settings, pyroptotic cell death. These findings position the NLRP3 inflammasome as a promising adjunctive therapeutic target in snakebite envenoming, although causal evidence remains restricted to selected toxin models and broader validation across venom classes is still required. This review summarizes the current understanding of NLRP3 inflammasome biology in the context of snake venoms and toxins, discusses the molecular mechanisms proposed for inflammasome priming and activation, and highlights unresolved questions relevant to toxinology, immunology, and adjunctive therapy development. Recent literature also places venom-derived molecules within the broader framework of NLRP3 inflammasome modulation, reinforcing the idea that venoms may serve both as drivers of pathology and as sources of pharmacological leads.

articles.title: Beyond Nanosizing: Mechanism-Guided Design and Rational Selection of Polymeric and Lipid Nanocarriers for Translatable Drug Delivery.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nanosizing can modify dissolution and carrier behaviour, but particle size alone does not determine clinically useful exposure. OBJECTIVE: To compare polymeric and lipid-based nanocarriers using a mechanism-guided framework that links payload properties, composition, process conditions, biological barriers, critical quality attributes (CQAs), and translational risk. METHODS: A critical narrative review with a structured scoping update was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar during manuscript preparation. The intended publication window was 2010-2025, with earlier seminal studies retained where mechanistically necessary. Because exact search dates, an auditable database export, screening counts, and independent-reviewer records were not preserved, this review is not presented as a systematic review and no pooled effect estimate is reported. RESULTS: Polymeric systems can stabilize selected amorphous or molecularly dispersed payloads and tune release through diffusion, hydration, and degradation, whereas lipid systems can support lipid-phase solubilization, digestion-dependent oral absorption, membrane interaction, and nucleic-acid delivery. Across both classes, precipitation, release failure, phase transformation, protein-corona and immune effects, endosomal sequestration, and process drift can disconnect favorable in vitro attributes from human pharmacology. Clinical examples show product-specific changes in disposition, safety, or efficacy rather than a universal bioavailability multiplier. CONCLUSION: Rational nanocarrier selection should start from a testable mechanism and a defined translational risk, then be challenged with route-relevant biological assays, exposure measurements, safety data, and manufacturing comparability. The proposed framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Snail-shRNA in AAV9 inhibited EMT and pulmonary fibrosis in silica-instilled mice.
articles.abstract: Our previous study in vitro has shown that targeting transcription factor Snail might be a strategy for the treatment of silicosis. In this study, we evaluated the feasibility of the strategy in vivo. Here we used CBG transgenic mice which could be used to track and isolate alveolar epithelial type II cells (AT II cells) to confirm that 2.5mg silica could induce epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in AT II cells in vivo. Based on the results that 2.5mg silica induced a rapid elevation of Snail in the lungs of mice and the optimal injection dose and stable expression time of adeno-associated virus (AAV) 9 vectors, we finally decided to inject AAV9-mediated Snail knockdown at 1.0×1011 vg/mouse 1 week before silica instillation to inhibit the levels of Snail increased by silica. The results showed that Snail-shRNA in AAV9 prevented silica-induced EMT in AT II cells in CBG transgenic mice and inhibited EMT and pulmonary fibrosis induced by silica in wild-type mice. Quantitative proteomic analysis combined with dbEMT database mapping further indicated that Snail knockdown suppressed silica-induced EMT and fibrosis through a Fibronectin (FN1)-centered interaction network involving proMMP8 activation and JUN kinase signaling. These findings suggested that Snail could be used as a target for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis in the future.

articles.title: An electrospun PCL/PVA-chitosan nanofiber scaffold loaded with selenium nanoparticles promotes antibacterial activity and accelerates wound healing: synthesis, characterization, and in-vivo evaluation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic, epidermal full-thickness wounds present a critical clinical challenge due to high risks of infection, impaired healing, and lack of advanced dressings that synergistically combine antibacterial efficacy with tissue regeneration. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to design and evaluate a multifunctional nanofibrous scaffold that simultaneously addresses anti-infection, mechanical support, and controlled tissue remodeling. METHODS: A tri-component nanofibrous scaffold composed of polyvinyl alcohol, chitosan, and polycaprolactone was fabricated via electrospinning. Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) were incorporated to impart antibacterial and pro-healing properties. The scaffold was characterized for morphological, mechanical, and biological attributes. In vivo performance was assessed using a murine epidermal full-thickness wound model. RESULTS: The scaffold demonstrated significantly enhanced mechanical properties and exhibited potent antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli. Controlled release of SeNPs reduced initial cytotoxic burst effects. In vivo tests confirmed accelerated wound closure and superior tissue regeneration compared to controls CONCLUSION: The SeNP-functionalized nanofibrous scaffold represents a promising therapeutic platform for epidermal full-thickness wound healing, effectively combining mechanical robustness, antibacterial action, and biocompatibility.
